audit_scope.description: These subgraphs cover CL fork transitions (Electra→Fulu), CL validator custody/data availability (PeerDAS), and EL history expiry (EIP-7927). Both layers and their interfaces are in scope.

out_of_scope_reasons.JSON-RPC API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty: vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Beacon API: Explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty: vulnerabilities requiring publicly exposed API
out_of_scope_reasons.Infrastructure bugs: Webpages, DNS, email etc. are out-of-scope
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration errors: Requires node operator error, not external attack
out_of_scope_reasons.High-effort DoS: Sustained, CPU or bandwidth intensive, and/or requires more than 1 packet or on-chain transaction
out_of_scope_reasons.ERC-20 contract bugs: Typically not included per Ethereum Bug Bounty
out_of_scope_reasons.ENS bugs: Maintained by ENS foundation, not in scope

misclassified_entities.reason: Beacon Chain State is an internal component of the CL, not an external entity. It is the state store within the system under audit.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Client via Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator clients query proposer lookahead via Beacon API. While typically co-located, the Beacon API is a defined interface boundary. However, Beacon API is out-of-scope for bug bounty, so vulnerabilities here are informational only.
trusted_external_entities.bug_bounty_note: Beacon API is explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty. Findings via this entry point are not eligible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL provides blob data, cell KZG proofs, and execution payloads to CL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated but data content (especially blob cells and KZG proofs) must be validated. A compromised or buggy EL could provide invalid cell proofs, causing invalid sidecar distribution.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peers via Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated peers on the P2P network publish and subscribe to data column sidecar topics. Any peer can send arbitrary data. All received sidecars must be fully validated before use.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peers via Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated peers request data column sidecars. Malicious peers could send crafted requests to exhaust resources or probe custody group assignments.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peers via DevP2P (eth/69)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EIP-7642 drops pre-merge fields from eth protocol. Peers on the P2P network are unauthenticated. Malicious peers could exploit protocol changes during the transition period.

trusted_external_entities.name: Portal Network Peers
trusted_external_entities.rationale: After history expiry (EIP-7927), pre-merge data may be retrieved from the Portal Network. Peers are unauthenticated and data must be validated against known block hashes.

trusted_external_entities.name: e2store Archive Source
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archive data source for pre-merge history. Data integrity must be verified against canonical block hashes. Source authenticity is not guaranteed.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External applications querying historical data. JSON-RPC is explicitly out-of-scope for bug bounty.
trusted_external_entities.bug_bounty_note: JSON-RPC API is explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty. Findings via this entry point are not eligible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Top-down archetypal threat: a malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or attempt to manipulate proposer lookahead by influencing randomness seeds. All validator messages must be fully validated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Response data (proposer lookahead) must be computed deterministically from beacon state. Beacon API is out-of-scope for bug bounty.

JWT authentication validates channel. CL MUST validate cell KZG proofs from EL before constructing and distributing DataColumnSidecars. Invalid proofs from a buggy EL could cause invalid sidecar propagation across the network.
Full validation of received DataColumnSidecars required: verify KZG proofs, check Merkle inclusion proofs, validate slot/block references, enforce rate limits per peer.
Validate all request parameters. Enforce rate limits. Only serve sidecars within custody groups and retention window. Prevent resource exhaustion from malicious requests.
Validate all protocol messages. Handle protocol version negotiation correctly. Reject messages with pre-merge fields after eth/69 activation. Prevent state confusion during protocol transition.
All retrieved block data must be validated against known canonical block hashes. Do not trust data content from unauthenticated Portal Network peers.
Validate block hashes and transaction roots against canonical chain. e2store files may be tampered with if sourced from untrusted locations.
Handle data unavailability gracefully after history expiry. Return appropriate errors. JSON-RPC is out-of-scope for bug bounty.
Full block and attestation validation required. Verify proposer is correct per lookahead. Detect and reject slashable messages. Validate fork version in signature domain post-Fulu fork.
